title: Gaussian limit for products of normalized sum laws
statement: Let $n\ge0$, and for each $m\ge0$ let $\nu_m$ be the law of $(m+1)^{-1/2}$ times the sum of $m+1$ independent uniform signs. For every bounded continuous $F:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R$, $\int F\,d\nu_m^{\otimes n}\to\int F\,d\gamma_n$ as $m\to\infty$, where $\gamma_n$ is standard Gaussian measure on $\mathbb R^n$.
hypotheses_covered: $F:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R$ is bounded and continuous
replaced: Let $\gamma_n$ be standard Gaussian measure on $\mathbb R^n$. Let $\nu_m$ be the law of the normalized sum of $m+1$ independent uniform signs. For every $n\ge0$ and bounded continuous $F:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R$, $\int F\,d\nu_m^{\otimes n}\to\int F\,d\gamma_n$ as $m\to\infty$.
